title: docs(pm-skill): land the intake family's eight platform readings under the +34 ceiling ruling
body:
Fixes #14133
Fixes #14694
Fixes #14743
Fixes #14778
Fixes #14798
Fixes #14605
Fixes #14898
Fixes #14445
Part of #15013

The second increment of the `platform-readings.md` intake. The first one landed
the corrections and reported that the family's additions did not fit the ratchet;
this one lands the eight readings under the ruling that sized them.

Attribution, as prose so it survives an edit: produced by Claude Code, session
`https://claude.ai/code/session_019RfFHiRCSs3JXLK4cwcfox`.

## The ruling this executes

Maintainer, live PM chat, 2026-09-04, decision batch 27, on the recommendation
presented for #15013 — verbatim and untranslated, adopting option A:

> 「同意」

The director record (comment 5535777772) states what that adopts, in its own
words:

> The ceiling for `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md` is
> raised **by the measured need, +34, to 358** — a named, sized raise under the
> ratchet's own maintainer exit. The ratchet script's raise cites this ruling
> verbatim in its comment, per the ratchet header's rule (a raised ceiling
> carries the maintainer decision that authorised it).
>
> The eight readings land as the intake flight wrote them (chain head +5 ·
> payload channel +5 · search query shape +3 · channel envelope +6 · queue
> instrument +8 · queue progress +2 · end-of-shift report +3 · body repair +2).
> The three retracted statements stay deleted.
>
> The +34 is a **ceiling of the raise**, not a target: if the eight readings land
> in fewer lines, the raise is the smaller number.

It is an ORDINARY raise: not a `CROSS_FILE_MOVES` entry, no other ceiling moves,
and no re-wrap of untouched paragraphs used as line funding (2026-08-17 rule).

## Per member, measured rather than estimated

Every reading was written in the file's own voice and wrapped by the gate's own
`wrapLine` — the canonical form, so no line can be over budget and no break can
land on one of the junctions that render as a space. 120 **bytes** per line, not
columns.

| member | reading | lines |
|---|---|--:|
| chain head #14133 | the page-number walk's hard 422 at offset ~9,900, and the `sort=created` `asc` + `desc` partition with its overlap proof | +5 |
| payload channel #14694 | the claim-bearing-field rule, and the absence rule for this channel | +5 |
| search query shape #14743 | no GitHub qualifiers in the query, scope by parameter, the query written as a sentence | +3 |
| channel envelope #14778 | try-the-other-channel on any refusal (+5); the label-removal carve-out (+1) | +6 |
| merge-queue instrument #14798 | queue-ref parent-tip position chain (+3); merge-driver caveat (+3); full-page zero (+2) | +8 |
| queue progress #14605 | the `event=merge_group` progress instrument and the batch-naming trap | +2 |
| end-of-shift report #14445 item 3 | `check_suite.completed` is a wake (+1); the tier script answers only its own tree (+2) | +3 |
| body repair #14898 | the raw-body source to repair from when the read itself is lossy | +2 |
| | **total** | **+34** |

+34 is the ruling's ceiling and this landed exactly at it, so the raise is +34 and
not less. Nothing was shortened to fit, and nothing was padded to reach it.

⚠️ **A note on the #14445 row, raised by this flight and since answered by the
seat.** The ruling and the dispatch both spell it `Fixes`, and this body follows
them. The flight flagged that the card is a shift-end report while only its item
③ is in this family, and asked whether the `Part of` spelling for that card
should be used instead, so that any unaddressed half would survive the merge. The
seat answered on the chain head: item ①1 was dispositioned on 2026-09-03, item ①2
was ruled KEPT on its own card, and item ② was routed — ③ was the only part still
outstanding, and it lands here. `Fixes` is correct and stays. Every other member
is single-fact and fully landed.

**Two of the twelve edits land without their emphasis markers.** Ten carry the
file's own bold convention; the label-removal carve-out and the merge-driver
caveat each cost one line MORE with theirs, which would have put the file at 360
— past the ruled ceiling. They land in the exact un-emphasised text the +34 was
measured on. Measured both ways: all-emphasis is +36, the landed mix is +34.

Deduped against `origin/main` before anything was written, exactly as the first
increment did: a fact the file already carries is cited, not re-spelled. The
three statements the first increment retracted stay deleted — reverse-checked by
grep on the landed tree.

## Ratchet verdict, before and after

Before, on `origin/main`:

```
✓ check-skill-line-ratchet: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md is 324 lines (ceiling 324; headroom 0).
```

After, at `581bc995`:

```
✓ check-skill-line-ratchet: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md is 358 lines (ceiling 358; headroom 0).
✓ check-skill-line-ratchet: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md: widest table row is 0 bytes (pin 0; headroom 0).
```

Headroom is **0**, the same convention every other entry in the map keeps.

## ⚠️ One thing the ruling could not have sized: the standing cross-file move

**This is the reviewer's decision point in this PR.** Raising the ceiling row
alone leaves the gate RED, and the reason is a mechanism the ruling did not reach.

The same entry carries a live `CROSS_FILE_MOVES` declaration — the readings
consolidation that set the 324 ceiling about a day earlier. Its `was: 314` is what
makes THAT move's raise computable from the tree. With the ceiling at 358 and
`was` left at 314, the gate reads the maintainer's independent +34 as though the
move had claimed it, and says so:

```
✗ check-skill-line-ratchet: cross-file move into .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md raises its ceiling 314→358 (+44) against a net source decrease of 11 (… cli.md 35→31, … services.md 30→28, … rest-channel.md 93→88). A move pays for itself by DELETION at the source; …
✗ check-skill-line-ratchet: the declared cross-file moves raise the map's total by 33 lines.
```

That verdict is not wrong about its own arithmetic — it is measuring a raise the
sources were never asked to pay for. The declaration's docblock anticipates a
later raise colliding with it and says the accounting belongs to the later raise's
author, holding the ruling; that is this PR. It writes the case for a later raise
at a SOURCE, so a raise at the DESTINATION is the shape it does not have words for.

**What this PR does:** carries the destination's baseline forward with the raise,
`was: 314` → `348` (= 314 + the ruled 34), with the reasoning written beside it.
Everything the declaration exists to guard is preserved, and the numbers are the
ones it landed with:

```
✓ check-skill-line-ratchet: cross-file move into …/platform-readings.md: +10 (348→358) against a net source decrease of 11 (…); authorised by #14685 item 5 (comment 5520452691).
✓ check-skill-line-ratchet: declared cross-file moves: 1, total ceilings down 1 line.
```

`+10` against `−11`, map total down one line — byte-for-byte the reading the move
landed with when the destination was at 324. A source that grows back still drives
the decrease under 10 and reds; the destination still reads PAID DOWN at or below
`was`. The reviewer's completeness check changes shape and the comment says so:
the SOURCES' `was` are still their `origin/main` values at `f3ae441fa2`, held
against that diff, while the DESTINATION's is that value plus every ordinary ruled
raise since — each carrying its own quoted ruling beside its ceiling.

**Alternatives, if the seat prefers one — each is a one-line change:** retire the
declaration (strictly weaker: it drops the source-regrowth guard the docblock was
written for), or teach the script to separate an ordinary raise from a move's
raise (a logic change to a governed script, which is a ruling, not an edit).
Nothing else in the map moved, and no new declaration was added.

## Measured and NOT landed: the three post-ruling facts

The three facts recorded on the chain head AFTER the ruling — comments 5533510809,
5533845391 and 5534733764 — are outside the +34 the ruling sized, so they are
measured here and left for a later increment.

| fact | where it would go | lines |
|---|---|--:|
| the attribution footer mutates per CHANNEL — the MCP wrapper deletes the block, a raw REST PATCH appends a bare one and leaves a session-URL footer intact (+58 bytes, prefix byte-identical), and comment creation appends the same 58 on both channels, so a strict parse of an `os-dev-report` comment must stop at the last closing brace | 读数陷阱, beside the existing PR-body footer bullet | +5 |
| the two write channels carry SEPARATE rate budgets and the MCP one is shared by identity, so an MCP refusal is a fact about that shared hourly window and not about this seat's; the two operations only MCP or GraphQL can do (draft flip, auto-merge) are unavailable for that window while everything else keeps flowing over REST | API 配额, after the 红窗调度 row | +6 |
| | **total** | **+11** |

Written in the file's voice and wrapped by the same `wrapLine`, so these are
landing costs, not estimates. The 5533845391 rows supersede 5533510809, which is
why they are one row here and not two. Landing them needs its own sizing decision;
this PR does not take it.

## The four prior-regime holds, read line by line against the landed file

Reported so the seat can close them on evidence. ⛔ No hold's text was edited into
the file: only facts among the eight landed. All four remain open here.

**#13373 remains open** — the payload channel drops the NEWEST timeline items past
the SSR first window (3 of 5 comments; front 15 edges of totalCount 21, back 0 of
21); proposed remedy was to compare rendered edges against `totalCount`.
- STATED at **L149**: the comment list is one of the two things the file now calls
  untrustworthy, with the same 15-item first window and a measured shape of the
  same kind (12 comments served as 3).
- STATED at **L152**: the in-band detector, in the file's own spelling — absence
  on this channel is not a reading unless `hasNextPage: false` or a second channel
  says so. Same mechanical test the card asked for, written as the flag the
  payload itself carries.
- NOT STATED: the card's per-half edge/`totalCount` arithmetic. The file states
  the rule, not that instance's numbers.
- ⇒ Superseded in substance. Closable on L149 + L152.

**#13385 remains open** — only the first 15 timeline items render and the tail
comes back EMPTY, so a read-back of a just-posted comment is byte-identical to
sanitizer damage; asked for option B, a discriminator.
- STATED at **L149**: the 15-item first window and `hasNextPage: true`, verbatim
  in the file's voice.
- STATED at **L152**: read your own just-written content back over the channel you
  wrote it on — the card's rule, with a broader predicate than its `get_comments`
  spelling.
- STATED at **L152**, and this is option B: the discriminator is `hasNextPage:
  false` or a second channel. Cheaper than the card's proposal, which needed a
  known-present earlier comment as a positive control.
- NOT STATED: the explicit page parameter spelling, and the anecdote that the
  reading looks exactly like sanitizer damage — carried in substance by 「本档的
  缺席不是读数」 plus the separate truncation-diagnosis bullet.
- ⇒ Superseded. Closable.

**#13387 remains open** — the payload is CDN-CACHED and can be minutes-to-hours
stale; a cache-buster query string and a no-cache header did NOT defeat it across
three fetches over 75 minutes. One seat asserted a half-state about another seat's
work on that read.
- STATED at **L152**: 「本档的缺席不是读数」 is the general form of the card's
  rule, and it covers the half-state and race-recheck instances by construction.
- STATED at **L151**: claim-bearing fields — `assignees`, `pm:*` labels, `state` —
  are never read from this channel, which is exactly the half-state case behind
  the card's damage report.
- PARTLY STATED at **L150**: "4–12 重取仍缺" records that a refetch does not
  repair the gap, but attributes it to the first-window truncation.
- **NOT STATED — a genuine residue**: the CAUSE. Nothing in the file says the
  channel is CDN-cached, or that a cache-buster plus a no-cache header was
  measured and did not defeat it. A reader gets the rule but cannot tell why
  re-fetching will not help, which is the one thing this card measured that the
  other two did not.
- ⇒ NOT fully superseded. One candidate line for a later increment; closable only
  if the seat judges the rule sufficient without the mechanism.

**#13257 remains open** — agent-created Routine transport: sessions fired by
`create_trigger` get no `mcp__github__*` tools (two probes, the second excluding
the competing explanation); self-binding wakes an existing session with its tools
loaded; `create_trigger` takes neither `sources` nor `model` and falls to the
default tier; agents cannot edit a UI-created Routine; and the orphan-timer
recovery path.
- NOT STATED, none of it. The only adjacent text is **L356**, the 断粮 section,
  which points at the main file for 定时器选型 and carries only `ccusage blocks`.
- ⇒ Entirely unaddressed. It is a different fact family from the eight, was never
  inside the ruling's sizing, and needs its own increment sized on its own.

## Scope held

- File surface: `platform-readings.md`, plus the one ceiling row with its quoted
  ruling and — declared above — the standing move declaration's baseline, in
  `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`. No other file.
- Facts whose home is `rest-channel.md` or `lanes/**` were not written anywhere.
- No other ceiling moved; no `CROSS_FILE_MOVES` entry was added; no re-wrap was
  used as funding. The two bullets the previous increment reported as unspent
  payment candidates are still unspent.

`check-governed-merges --test` on this PR's two paths returns its GOVERNED verdict
(exit 3 = `EXIT_TEST_GOVERNED`), naming `.claude/**` as the hit:

```
⛔  GOVERNED — a human merge is the review record for this PR (#9495 regime).
```

**NOT MEASURED, then repaired to a real verdict:** `check:doc-formula-expressions`
first exited **3** with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the workspace package
@objectstack/formula is not built`, then again with the same for
`@objectstack/lint`. Exit 3 is not a finding; both packages were built through the
shared verify lock and the gate re-ran to the green verdict quoted above. Heavy
runs went through `bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c` (VERDICT command-exit 0;
held 70s, 40s and 354s across three batches, waited 0s / 0s / 0s, and 70s waited on
one build — shared-box seconds, as the lock's own verdict line states).

**`pnpm lint` — a proven narrowing, not a skip.** Repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`
is CI's run. Locally the two changed paths were linted directly, and the narrowing
is measured on all three legs the discipline asks for:

1. **The population comes from eslint's own config, not a guess.** The markdown
   file comes back `File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied` —
   eslint's config puts `.md` outside its population entirely, so the only path of
   this diff eslint judges at all is the `.mjs`.
2. **The count comes from `--format json`:** 2 entries returned, 1 judged, **0
   errors, 0 warnings** on `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`, exit 0.
3. **Invariance over untouched files:** this repo runs one `eslint.config.mjs`
   which, in its own words at line 327, "never enables type-aware linting (no
   `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for ANY file".
   With no cross-file type program, a two-file diff cannot move the verdict on a
   file it does not contain.

**One name in the dispatch does not exist in this repo:** `pnpm check:control-bytes`
has no such script. The control-byte gate is spelled `check:nul-bytes`, it is in
the derived family, and it ran green above. The two changed files were also swept
directly for raw control bytes outside the gate — no hits.

The ratchet script's own test suite is its `--self-test` (136 cases, green above);
a repo-wide grep over `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` for `skill-line-ratchet` returns no
dedicated test file, so nothing else is owed on that leg.

## Merge path

`.claude/**` is a governed surface. **Draft, human merge.** Not flipped ready, no
auto-merge, no reviewers requested — the ruling puts the review request for
`os-zhuang` and `hotlong` with the seat, not with this flight. `skip-changeset`
applies: nothing is published from any package.
